lessons.lesson: A required-arm flag is a demand, not a preference: without pinning the rank the gate can admit the arm and a different one can still serve, and the honest failure is a non-zero exit rather than a silent substitution. Pin the rank whenever the owner names a model.
lessons.applied_to: two lanes re-dispatched with force-rank 2 and the mandated arm; both then served it

lessons.lesson: Freeze facts, not summaries. A checker handed only an inventory of paths cannot establish additivity or head binding; the first verdict said so, and the second cleared those checks only after the contents and the branch tips were supplied.
lessons.applied_to: PR_FACTS2.json plus the repair note; V2 and V4 moved from unverifiable to clear

lessons.lesson: A gate you write binds you. This round's own repair note said to hold the merges if a published artefact carried a credential-shaped string, and the checker held on exactly that. Writing a narrow gate and then ignoring it would be worse than never writing one.
lessons.applied_to: both merges held and recorded in MERGE_DECISION.json

lessons.lesson: Weigh a finding by its context, not its shape. The flagged strings are a scanner's synthetic positive controls, which exist to prove the scanner works; that is a disclosure to make, not an undetected credential. Publishing the disclosure is the correct handling.
lessons.applied_to: ER-2-5 and the V6 finding as published

lessons.lesson: Read-only lanes cannot deliver files. A verdict that only exists in stdout is still a verdict; transcribe it mechanically with the stream hash and say so.
lessons.applied_to: PLAN notes and both VERIFY verdicts

lessons.lesson: Line endings are part of the change. A CFRL copy of an LF file turns a two-line insertion into a whole-file rewrite that no reviewer can read; the opcode check is what proves additivity.
